title: Electric Circuits 2
objectives: The main objective of Electric Circuits 2 is to cover fundamental theoretical principles and practical applications.
syllabus:
Network graphs, the concept of loop and cut set in terms of their matrix expression,
Telegan's theorem, input impedance properties, mesh node analysis methods in general
linear circuits, including writing the mesh node equations in the form of a matrix with a
regular, mental and shortcut method. Dual graphs and circuits, the concept of tree and
branch along with the tree and their relationship in determining disconnected loops and
cutsets
in a graph and determining disconnected variables of voltage and branch current in a
circuit. State space method, matrix representation of state equations, approximate
determination of the path of state space and state equations in linear and nonlinear circuits,
Laplace transform and its applications, frequency domain analysis of electrical circuits, basic
properties of linear circuits invariant with time, natural frequencies of a network and a
variable network and its determination both in time domain and in frequency domain,
network functions of its poles and zeros, determination of frequency response of drawing
brush, basic review of circuit theorems including substitution theorem, sum of effects
theorem, Tonen-Norten equivalent circuit theorem, co-response theorem in its different
forms. Dipoles and how to specify bipolar circuits with Z, Y, H and T parameters, connecting
dipoles and multipoles.
textbooks:
1- W. H. Hayt, J. E. Kemmerly, and S. M. Durbin, Engineering Circuit Analysis, 8th Edition,
McGraw Hill, 2011.
2- C. K. Alexander, M. N. O. Sadiku, Fundamentals of Electrical Circuits, 5th Edition,
McGraw Hill, 2012
3- A. Agarwal, J. H. Lang, Foundations of Analog and Digital Electronic Circuits, Morgan
Kaufmann Publishers, Elsevier, 2005
